name: Siege of Baghdad (1258)
note: The plan shows the whole operation, not a single field. The compass directions are only roughly given by the accounts, and the places the Mongol columns started from are placed by judgement. The moat, palisade and pontoon bridges were built after the first phases but are drawn throughout; the accounts do not say exactly where they lay. The surrender is drawn as the garrison leaving the field, not as its destruction.

phases.title: The Mongol columns approach Baghdad
phases.text: Hulegu led the main force, with the Golden Horde princes on the right and Kitbuqa on the left. After a council of war in mid-December Baiju returned to the vanguard at Irbil, while Baghdad held a garrison of its own.
phases.quote: his commanders dispersed to carry out different tasks

phases.title: Baiju crosses at Mosul and marches south
phases.text: Baiju crossed the Tigris at Mosul with the help of its emir and headed south. He reached the Nahr Isa canal, and his deputy Sughunchaq pushed the advance party to about 40 km from the city.
phases.quote: Baiju reached the Nahr Isa canal in mid-January 1258, whereupon his deputy Sughunchaq pushed the advance party

phases.title: The dawatdar's army marches out
phases.text: The dawatdar met the advance party with 20,000 infantry and forced it to retreat, and the caliphal army pursued.
phases.quote: On 16 January, Sughunchaq was confronted by the dawatdar with 20,000 infantry and forced to retreat

phases.title: The canal dykes are broken and the camp flooded
phases.text: That night Baiju's forces broke the dykes of the Dujayl Canal and flooded the camp of the celebrating Abbasid army. Many drowned.
phases.quote: that night Baiju's forces broke the dykes of the Dujayl Canal and flooded the camp of the celebrating Abbasid army

phases.title: Baiju's army routs the survivors
phases.text: Baiju's army engaged the remainder the next morning. They were routed, and only a few, the dawatdar among them, got back to Baghdad.
phases.quote: the remainder were engaged by Baiju's army the following morning

phases.title: Hulegu and Kitbuqa close in on the city
phases.text: Kitbuqa crossed the Tigris to the south and approached the Karkh suburbs, while Hulegu reached the eastern suburbs. The Mongols then enclosed the whole city with a palisade and a moat, completed within a day.
phases.quote: Hulegu himself reached the eastern suburbs on 22 January

phases.title: The first breach is driven back
phases.text: The assault on the walls began on 29 or 30 January. The first breach, in the southeast Ajami tower near Hulegu's camp, was made on 1 February, but the Mongols were driven back.
phases.quote: but the Mongols were driven back

phases.title: The Mongols take the east battlements
phases.text: Further breaches over the next two days let the Mongols reach the east battlements, and they seized control of them by 4 February.
phases.quote: further breaches over the next two days enabled them to access and seize control of the east battlements by 4 February

phases.title: The dawatdar tries to escape by river
phases.text: The dawatdar sailed down the Tigris to escape. The Mongol preparations on the river held and forced him back into the city with a loss of three ships.
phases.quote: the dawatdar attempted to escape by sailing down the Tigris

phases.title: Unarmed men who came out are executed
phases.text: A large number of unarmed soldiers and inhabitants came out of the city, apparently hoping to be spared and allowed to settle in Syria. They were divided into groups and executed.
phases.quote: a large number of unarmed soldiers and inhabitants emerged from the city

phases.title: The caliph surrenders the city
phases.text: After envoys had failed to win terms, the caliph surrendered the city on 10 February, bringing his family and 3,000 dignitaries.
phases.quote: the caliph surrendered on 10 February, bringing his family and 3,000 dignitaries
